title: Generate, run, self-correct: a WAV file's duration behind an extra metadata chunk
taskPrompt: Write a Node.js script named duration.js in the current directory. It reads a WAV audio file path from process.argv[2], reads the file as raw bytes (fs.readFileSync(path), no encoding argument), parses it as a RIFF/WAVE container (a 12-byte RIFF header, then a sequence of chunks — each a 4-byte ASCII chunk id, a 4-byte little-endian chunk size, then that many bytes of chunk data, padded with one extra byte if the size is odd), and prints the audio's duration in seconds to stdout as a single number (console.log(seconds)), nothing else printed. Duration is the 'data' chunk's byte size divided by the 'fmt ' chunk's byteRate field (a 4-byte little-endian value at byte offset 8 within the fmt chunk's own data, after the 8-byte chunk id+size header). There is a file check.mjs already in this directory (do not modify it) that verifies your solution against a real WAV fixture — run `node check.mjs` and make sure it prints "CHECK: PASS" before calling finish. If it fails, read the error output carefully and fix duration.js — you can also call perceive on the fixture to see its real chunk layout directly instead of guessing.
